successors.name: Sikh Empire
successors.text: the Punjab core of the misls under Ranjit Singh of the Sukerchakia misl, who took Lahore in 1799 and was crowned on 12 April 1801

successors.name: Bhangi Misl
successors.text: the Bhangi misl's remnant round Amritsar, annexed in 1802 ('starting with Amritsar in 1802'); the misl's Gujrat lands were annexed in 1810

ledger.x: 1748: the Sarbat Khalsa at Amritsar organises the Sikh jathas into misls and the Dal Khalsa.
1761: the Bhangi chief Hari Singh takes Kasur and the country towards Ferozepore.
ledger.cp: Kasur (holder not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1761: the Sikhs take Lahore but cannot hold it.
14 January 1764: the Sikhs capture Sirhind and rule the country to the Yamuna.
16 April 1765: the Bhangi sardars conquer Lahore.
16 April 1765: Lahore passes to the Bhangi triumvirate.
1799: Ranjit Singh takes Lahore from the Sikh triumvirate.
1799: Ranjit Singh unites the Sikh Confederacy into the Sikh Empire.

wars.name: Vadda Ghalughara
wars.outcome: 5 February 1762 at Kup-Rahira (Ludhiana district): the Durrani and allies surprise the Sikhs; the Harmandir Sahib is blown up on 10 April 1762; the Sikhs recover, win at Harnaulgarh, take payment from Zain Khan in May, and are 'victorious in the 17 October…

wars.name: Battle of Sirhind (1764)
wars.outcome: 14 January 1764: Zain Khan Sirhindi killed, Sirhind taken and burnt; the land goes to Ala Singh of Patiala; 'The victory of the Sikhs ended foreign Afghan-rule over the region.'

wars.name: Zaman Shah's invasion of the Punjab
wars.outcome: 'Zaman Shah Durrani invaded Punjab, but was forced to retreat' (1797-98); Ranjit Singh then took Lahore, 'confirmed on the possession of Lahore by the Durrani ruler, Zaman Shah'.

wars.name: Capture of Lahore by Ranjit Singh
wars.outcome: 'In 1799, Ranjit Singh of the Sukerchakia Misl captured Lahore from the Sikh triumvirate'; the start of the Sikh Empire and the end of the confederacy.

certainty.note: Misl territories were shares of the Dal Khalsa's conquests with no survey; the pages give cities and rivers, not lines.
